segments.say: Somewhere in the distance, a clock strikes midnight, and a new year begins. A few fireworks bloom and fade far away, then the night grows quiet again. In the house, everything is still. The fire glows softly. The box of diaries rests by the chair. And there's nothing left to do now, nothing at all, except rest. You can let the night hold you, just as it holds the quiet house.

Imagine you're lying in a soft bed, under a warm, heavy blanket. The room is dark, except for a faint glow at the edge of the curtains. The sheets are cool at first, then slowly warm around you. Your head sinks a little into the pillow. Your body grows heavier. And outside the window, the night is calm and patient, with all the time in the world.

Tonight, there's no need to know what time it is. There's no alarm you need to think about, and no list you need to check. Time can wait outside the door, like a quiet friend who knows you need to rest. Whatever the clock says, this moment is yours. Let it stretch, slow and soft, for as long as you like.

Let's settle in together. A heavy head, resting on the pillow. Soft shoulders, sinking down. A slow breath, coming and going on its own. And a quiet mind, with nothing it needs to hold on to. If thoughts drift by, that's fine. Let them pass like clouds, without following them. They'll find their own way out of the sky.

Let's breathe together again for a little while. In through the nose, slowly, for four. One. Two. Three. Four. And out through the mouth, softly, for six. One. Two. Three. Four. Five. Six. Again. In for four. And out for six. With each breath out, let a little more of the day drift away from you.

show.sub: In for four, out for six

segments.say: Now let your breathing find its own rhythm. You don't need to count anymore. Just notice it, like the tide on a quiet shore. Coming in, gently. Going out, slowly. Coming in. Going out. The tide has been doing this for a very long time, long before any clock was made. It never rushes, and it never stops. And neither does your breath.

Picture a quiet shore under the moon. Small waves roll in, spread out across the smooth sand, and slide back again, leaving a thin silver line. Then another wave comes, and another, unhurried and soft. There's no one here but you, and the sea, and the moon. And the sound of the waves is the slowest, gentlest music in the world.

Let's bring a little attention to your body now, slowly, from the top down. Notice your forehead, and let it smooth out. Notice the small muscles around your eyes, and let them soften. Let your jaw loosen, so your teeth are slightly apart. Let your tongue rest. And let your shoulders drop, just a little further, as if someone had lifted a heavy bag from them.

Now let that softness flow down into your arms. Your upper arms, heavy and relaxed. Your elbows. Your forearms, resting. And your hands, lying open and still. Maybe you can feel a gentle warmth in your palms, or a faint tingle in your fingertips. There's nothing your hands need to hold tonight. Let them rest completely.

Here's a quiet thought to rest with. There is time enough for rest. Whatever the year has been, however fast it seemed to fly, this moment is slow and wide. You don't need to catch up with anything. You don't need to make up for lost time. Right now, there's time enough, just to lie here and breathe.

show.text: There is time enough for rest.

segments.say: Now notice your chest, gently rising and falling. And your belly, softening with each breath. Let your back sink into the bed, every part of it supported, from your shoulders to your hips. The bed is holding you. You don't need to hold yourself up at all. Let the weight of your body be carried, completely, the way the sea carries a floating leaf.

Let that heaviness flow down through your hips, into your legs. Your thighs, relaxed. Your knees. Your calves, soft and heavy. Your ankles. And your feet, warm and still, perhaps tucked under the blanket. Your whole body, from head to toe, is resting now. Heavy, warm and quiet. And there's nothing at all that you need to do.

Let's gently gather it all together. A smooth forehead. A soft jaw. Heavy arms. A slow, easy breath. And warm feet. Your whole body, resting in the dark. If any part of you still feels tense, just breathe toward it, softly, and let it loosen in its own time. There's no hurry. There's never any hurry here.

Now let your ears wander a little. Perhaps there's the hum of a fridge somewhere in the house. A car passing far away on a wet road. The soft tick of a radiator cooling. Or perhaps nothing at all, just a deep and gentle silence. Whatever you hear, let it be part of the night. Each sound comes, and goes, and leaves you a little more relaxed.

You can let your thoughts drift now, wherever they like. Perhaps to a place you love. Perhaps to nowhere in particular. You don't need to follow the story anymore, or remember anything. If you fall asleep in the middle of a sentence, that's perfect. That's what tonight is for. My voice will keep going, softly, like rain on a roof, keeping you company.

And in a moment, we'll take a slow walk together, through a quiet winter town, where the snow is falling and the bells are far away. There's nowhere we need to get to. We'll just wander, gently, and let the night unfold around us. But there's no rush to begin. Take another slow breath first. In. And out. And let's go.
